topics.name: Snowflake AI Data Cloud Features and Architecture
topics.description: Snowflake's multi-cluster shared-data architecture, editions, interfaces and tools, object hierarchy, virtual warehouses, storage concepts, and AI/ML and application development features.

subtopics.name: Snowflake Architecture and Editions
subtopics.description: The three architectural layers and how Snowflake editions differ.
keyPoints: Cloud Services layer coordinates authentication, metadata, query optimization, and access control
Compute (query processing) layer runs queries on independent virtual warehouses
Database Storage layer holds compressed, columnar micro-partitions
Storage and compute scale independently in a multi-cluster shared-data architecture
Editions (Standard, Enterprise, Business Critical, Virtual Private Snowflake) differ in features, security, and compliance
subtopics.content:
Snowflake's architecture separates **storage**, **compute**, and **cloud services** so each scales independently.

- **Cloud Services** — authentication, metadata, the query optimizer, and access control.
- **Compute** — virtual warehouses that process queries; add more warehouses without contending for the same resources.
- **Storage** — data persisted as compressed, columnar micro-partitions in cloud object storage.

> Editions (Standard → Enterprise → Business Critical → VPS) layer on additional security, compliance, and features rather than more compute.

subtopics.name: Interfaces and Tools
keyPoints: Snowsight is the web interface for queries, worksheets, and visualization
Snowflake CLI provides command-line access to the platform
IDE integrations such as Visual Studio Code connect to Snowflake
Multiple interfaces share the same underlying account and objects
subtopics.content:
You can reach the same account and objects through multiple interfaces:

- **Snowsight** — the modern web UI for worksheets, dashboards, and monitoring.
- **Snowflake CLI** and **SnowSQL** — command-line access for scripting and automation.
- **Drivers & IDE integrations** (e.g. the VS Code extension) — connect tools and applications.

subtopics.name: Object Hierarchy and Types
subtopics.description: Organization/account objects, database objects, and session context.
keyPoints: Organization and account objects sit above databases
Database objects include stages, schemas, tables, views, UDFs, file formats, stored procedures, pipes, shares, sequences, ML models, and applications
Session and context variables follow a parameter hierarchy and precedence (account, user, session)
Fully-qualified names resolve objects as database.schema.object
subtopics.content:
Objects are organized in a hierarchy. Organization and account objects sit above **databases**, which contain **schemas**, which contain tables, views, stages, file formats, UDFs, procedures, pipes, streams, tasks, and more.

Resolve objects with fully-qualified names: `database.schema.object`. Parameters follow a precedence order of **account → user → session**.

subtopics.name: Virtual Warehouses
keyPoints: Warehouse types include Standard (Gen 1 and Gen 2) and Snowpark-optimized
Sizing (up/down) changes per-cluster compute; scaling (in/out) with multi-cluster handles concurrency
Auto-suspend and auto-resume control cost by pausing idle compute
Scaling policies (Standard, Economy) govern multi-cluster start/stop behavior
Match warehouse configuration to workloads: ad-hoc queries, data loading, BI and reporting
subtopics.content:
A **virtual warehouse** is the compute that runs queries.

- **Sizing (up/down)** changes per-cluster power for heavier queries.
- **Scaling (in/out)** with multi-cluster warehouses handles more concurrent users.
- **Auto-suspend / auto-resume** pause idle compute to control cost.

Billing is per-second with a 60-second minimum whenever a warehouse is running.

subtopics.name: Storage Concepts
keyPoints: Data is stored in immutable, compressed, columnar micro-partitions
Micro-partition metadata enables pruning to skip irrelevant data
Data clustering and clustering keys improve pruning on large tables
Table types: permanent, temporary, transient, external, dynamic, and Apache Iceberg
View types: standard, materialized, and secure
subtopics.content:
Data lives in immutable, compressed, columnar **micro-partitions**. Snowflake automatically keeps metadata (min/max, distinct counts) per micro-partition, enabling **pruning** — skipping partitions that cannot match a query.

On very large tables, a **clustering key** keeps related data co-located to improve pruning. Choose table types deliberately: permanent, temporary, transient, external, dynamic, or Apache Iceberg.

subtopics.name: AI/ML and Application Development Features
subtopics.description: Snowflake features for AI, ML, and app development.
keyPoints: Snowflake Notebooks and Streamlit in Snowflake support interactive development and apps
Snowpark runs custom Python, Java, and Scala code inside Snowflake
Snowflake Cortex provides AI SQL functions, Cortex Search, and Cortex Analyst
Snowflake ML supports model development and deployment on the platform
subtopics.content:
Snowflake supports building AI/ML and apps close to the data:

- **Snowpark** runs Python, Java, and Scala inside Snowflake.
- **Notebooks** and **Streamlit in Snowflake** enable interactive development and apps.
- **Cortex** offers AI SQL functions, Cortex Search, and Cortex Analyst.

topics.name: Account Management and Data Governance
topics.description: Snowflake's security model, data governance features, and monitoring and cost management.

subtopics.name: Security Model and Principles
keyPoints: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): privileges granted to roles, roles granted to users
Discretionary Access Control (DAC): the owning role can grant access to its objects
System-defined roles include ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN, USERADMIN, SYSADMIN, and PUBLIC
Functional roles include account roles, database roles, and custom roles; secondary roles broaden active privileges
Authentication options: MFA, federated authentication, SSO, OAuth, and key-pair authentication
Network policies restrict access by IP; logging and tracing capture activity
subtopics.content:
Access is governed by **RBAC**: privileges are granted to **roles**, and roles are granted to **users** (and to other roles to form hierarchies). Snowflake also uses **DAC**, where the owning role can grant access to its objects.

Know the system roles — **ACCOUNTADMIN**, **SECURITYADMIN**, **USERADMIN**, **SYSADMIN**, **PUBLIC** — and authentication options: MFA, SSO/federation, OAuth, and key-pair.

subtopics.name: Data Governance Features
subtopics.description: Masking, classification, tagging, lineage, and protection.
keyPoints: Dynamic Data Masking and row access policies enforce column- and row-level security
Data classification automatically detects and labels sensitive data; object tagging categorizes objects
Privacy policies and the Trust Center support governance and security posture review
Encryption key management provides end-to-end encryption with key rotation
Alerts, notifications, data lineage, and data replication and failover support governance
subtopics.content:
Governance features protect and describe data:

- **Dynamic Data Masking** and **row access policies** enforce column- and row-level security.
- **Data classification** and **object tagging** label and categorize sensitive data.
- **Data lineage**, the **Trust Center**, and end-to-end **encryption with key rotation** round out the posture.

subtopics.name: Monitoring and Cost Management
keyPoints: Resource monitors track warehouse credit usage and can suspend at thresholds, at no additional cost
Virtual warehouse credit usage depends on size and runtime (billed per second, 60-second minimum)
The ACCOUNT_USAGE schema exposes account-wide usage and metadata views
Cost and warehouse monitoring helps control spend
subtopics.content: **Resource monitors** track warehouse credit usage and can notify or suspend when thresholds are hit — at no extra cost. The **ACCOUNT_USAGE** schema exposes account-wide usage and metadata for cost analysis.

topics.name: Data Loading, Unloading, and Connectivity
topics.description: Loading and unloading data, automated ingestion, and Snowflake connectors and integrations.

subtopics.name: Data Loading and Unloading
subtopics.description: Stages, COPY, file formats, and error handling.
keyPoints: File formats define how data is parsed (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, ORC, XML)
Stages can be internal (user, table, named) or external (S3, Azure, GCS) and support directory tables
COPY INTO <table> bulk loads staged files; COPY INTO <location> unloads data
PUT uploads local files to an internal stage; GET downloads files from a stage
Error handling with ON_ERROR (CONTINUE, SKIP_FILE, ABORT_STATEMENT) controls load behavior
Load metadata prevents reloading the same file
subtopics.content:
Bulk data movement centers on **stages**, **file formats**, and **COPY**:

- **Stages** can be internal (user/table/named) or external (S3/Azure/GCS).
- `COPY INTO <table>` loads staged files; `COPY INTO <location>` unloads.
- `PUT` uploads to an internal stage; `GET` downloads.
- `ON_ERROR` (CONTINUE / SKIP_FILE / ABORT_STATEMENT) controls load behavior; load metadata prevents reloading the same file.

subtopics.name: Automated Data Ingestion
keyPoints: Snowpipe loads data continuously in micro-batches as files arrive (serverless)
Snowpipe Streaming ingests rows with low latency without staging files
Streams track table changes (CDC) for incremental processing
Tasks schedule and orchestrate SQL and can be chained into DAGs
Dynamic tables declaratively maintain transformed results
subtopics.content:
For continuous ingestion:

- **Snowpipe** loads files in micro-batches as they arrive (serverless).
- **Snowpipe Streaming** ingests rows with low latency, no staging.
- **Streams** track changes (CDC); **Tasks** schedule SQL and chain into DAGs; **Dynamic Tables** declaratively maintain transformed results.

subtopics.name: Connectors and Integrations
keyPoints: Snowflake drivers (JDBC, ODBC, Python, etc.) enable programmatic connectivity
Snowflake connectors integrate with external systems such as Kafka and Spark
Storage integrations securely reference external cloud storage without credentials in SQL
API integration and Git integration connect external services and repositories
subtopics.content: Connect programmatically with **drivers** (JDBC, ODBC, Python, Node.js, Go, .NET). **Connectors** integrate systems such as Kafka and Spark. **Storage integrations** reference external cloud storage without embedding credentials in SQL; **API** and **Git** integrations connect external services and repositories.

topics.name: Performance Optimization, Querying, and Transformation
topics.description: Evaluating and optimizing query performance, Snowflake caching, and data transformation techniques.

subtopics.name: Evaluate Query Performance
subtopics.description: Query Profile, ACCOUNT_USAGE views, and workload management.
keyPoints: Query Profile surfaces bytes spilled to storage, inefficient pruning, exploding joins, and queuing
SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE views provide query history and query attribution
Workload management best practices include grouping similar workloads on dedicated warehouses
Spilling to local or remote storage indicates an undersized warehouse
subtopics.content: Use the **Query Profile** to diagnose slow queries — watch for bytes **spilled** to local/remote storage, poor **pruning**, **exploding joins**, and **queuing**. The **ACCOUNT_USAGE** query history and query attribution views help track trends. Spilling usually signals an undersized warehouse.

subtopics.name: Optimize Query Performance
subtopics.description: Services and structures that speed up queries.
keyPoints: Query Acceleration Service offloads parts of eligible scan-heavy queries
Search Optimization Service speeds up selective point-lookup queries
Clustering keys improve pruning on large tables with well-chosen columns
Materialized views precompute and store query results for fast reads
subtopics.content:
Speed-up options, chosen by workload:

- **Query Acceleration Service** — offloads parts of scan-heavy queries.
- **Search Optimization Service** — accelerates selective point lookups.
- **Clustering keys** — improve pruning on large tables.
- **Materialized views** — precompute and store results for fast reads.

subtopics.name: Snowflake Caching
keyPoints: Query result cache returns identical results without recompute for 24 hours (extendable)
Metadata cache in the cloud services layer answers metadata-only queries instantly
Warehouse (local disk) cache holds recently accessed micro-partition data per warehouse
Result cache is independent of any running warehouse
subtopics.content:
Three cache layers reduce work:

1. **Result cache** — returns identical query results for 24 hours (extendable), independent of any warehouse.
2. **Metadata cache** — answers metadata-only queries instantly from cloud services.
3. **Warehouse (local disk) cache** — holds recently accessed micro-partition data per warehouse.

subtopics.name: Data Transformation Techniques
subtopics.description: Working with structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data.
keyPoints: Query structured, semi-structured (VARIANT, FLATTEN), and unstructured data
Aggregate functions summarize data across groups
Window functions compute across ordered partitions without collapsing rows
Apply SQL techniques to optimize transformation queries
subtopics.content: Transform structured and **semi-structured** data (VARIANT with `FLATTEN`), plus unstructured data. **Aggregate functions** summarize across groups; **window functions** compute across ordered partitions without collapsing rows.

topics.name: Data Collaboration
topics.description: Data protection features, Snowflake's data sharing capabilities, and sharing via the Marketplace and listings.

subtopics.name: Data Collaboration and Protection
subtopics.description: Cloning, Time Travel, Fail-safe, and replication.
keyPoints: Zero-copy cloning creates instant, metadata-only copies of databases, schemas, and tables
Time Travel queries or restores historical data within the retention period (up to 90 days on Enterprise)
Fail-safe provides a non-configurable 7-day Snowflake-managed recovery window after Time Travel expires
Data replication and failover support business continuity across regions and clouds
subtopics.content:
Continuous data protection features:

- **Zero-copy cloning** — instant, metadata-only copies of databases, schemas, and tables.
- **Time Travel** — query/restore historical data within the retention period (up to 90 days on Enterprise).
- **Fail-safe** — a non-configurable 7-day Snowflake-managed recovery window after Time Travel expires.
- **Replication & failover** — business continuity across regions and clouds.

subtopics.name: Data Sharing Capabilities
keyPoints: Secure Data Sharing shares live data with no data copy via provider and consumer accounts
Reader accounts let non-Snowflake consumers access shared data
Direct shares, sharing and resharing, and data clean rooms enable collaboration
Shared data is read-only for consumers and reflects provider updates in real time
subtopics.content: **Secure Data Sharing** shares live, read-only data with **no copy** between provider and consumer accounts — consumers always see current data. **Reader accounts** let non-Snowflake consumers access shared data. **Direct shares**, resharing, and **data clean rooms** enable richer collaboration.

subtopics.name: Marketplace and Listings
keyPoints: The Snowflake Marketplace publishes data and applications to consumers
Listings can be private (targeted) or public (broadly discoverable)
Native Apps distribute application logic alongside data
Marketplace listings build on Secure Data Sharing
subtopics.content: The **Snowflake Marketplace** publishes data and applications to consumers. **Listings** can be private (targeted) or public (broadly discoverable), and **Native Apps** distribute application logic alongside data. Marketplace listings are built on Secure Data Sharing.
